lineage.reason: 'Stronger, faster, better' paraphrases the well-known Six Million Dollar Man catchphrase 'better, stronger, faster'.
lineage.before: Stronger, faster, better looking. Obviously.
lineage.after: Fresh torque. Same genius. Still modest.

lineage.reason: 'That one was personal' leans on the well-known tagline 'This time it's personal', and the line has no Rigs flavour.
lineage.before: Ow. Okay, that one was personal.
lineage.after: Ow. Hull's cracked. Send patches, plural.

lineage.reason: 'Come get some' is a well-known catchphrase (Army of Darkness / Duke Nukem).
lineage.before: Come get some, tin cans!
lineage.after: Tin cans incoming. More scrap for me.

lineage.reason: 'Yippee-ki-yay' is the Die Hard catchphrase.
lineage.before: Yippee-ki-yay, Kessler-Voss. Thanks for the ore.
lineage.after: Full payload, full cut. Cheers, Kessler-Voss.

lineage.reason: 'Mama needs a new gun' paraphrases the well-known catchphrase 'Mama needs a new pair of shoes'.
lineage.before: Jackpot! Mama needs a new gun.
lineage.after: Jackpot! My cut just got bigger.

lineage.reason: 'Try not to overthink' is aimed at the player's choice rather than at Rook's plans or bravado.
lineage.before: Pick one. Try not to overthink.
lineage.after: Pick one. Think first, unlike Ceres.

lineage.reason: Mocking the failed run ('expensive nap') targets the player's performance, not Rook's plans.
lineage.before: Well. That was a very expensive nap.
lineage.after: Well. Still not as bad as Ceres.

lineage.reason: Propaganda aimed at an intruder event, and it sells the Rigs' own console as a Kessler-Voss product; label propaganda and text both must change to bureaucratic.
lineage.before: Kessler-Voss Smart Consoles: innovation, delivered straight to your doorstep!
lineage.after: Foreign device connected to claim network. Entry point recorded.

lineage.reason: 'Form 27-B' echoes the famous 'Form 27B/6' of the film Brazil, and 'retrieval' misdescribes a console being dropped.
lineage.before: Unauthorized console retrieval will be logged under Form 27-B.
lineage.after: Network intrusion at claim perimeter. Incident filed against unauthorized personnel.

lineage.reason: Playful propaganda ('Surprise!', 'valued guests') aimed at intruders instead of cold bureaucracy; change label and text to bureaucratic.
lineage.before: Surprise! A Kessler-Voss Rewards Crate has arrived for valued guests!
lineage.after: Cargo crate deployed on claim. Removal of contents will be invoiced.

lineage.reason: 'Compliance is mandatory' indirectly orders the player to stop instead of stating what the company does.
lineage.before: Security response dispatched. Compliance is mandatory and appreciated.
lineage.after: Security units dispatched to claim. Extraction irregularity scheduled for removal.

lineage.reason: Jokey propaganda ('coming to meet you!') aimed at intruders; change label and text to bureaucratic.
lineage.before: Kessler-Voss Safety Team is coming to meet you!
lineage.after: Claim defense units activated. Unauthorized personnel located and logged.

lineage.reason: Propaganda thanking intruders for visiting, and the company speaks as if it hosts the Rigs' shuttle; change label and text to bureaucratic.
lineage.before: Your premium departure experience awaits. Thank you for visiting!
lineage.after: Unregistered craft detected at landing site. Recovery crew notified.

lineage.reason: Threatens the player's exit instead of stating what the company does (reinforcements arriving).
lineage.before: Departure window closing. Late exits will be processed as trespass.
lineage.after: Extraction crews en route. Trespass filings prepared for personnel on site.

lineage.reason: Paraphrases the Scarface line 'Say hello to my little friend'.
lineage.before: Say hello to my little friend, but louder.
lineage.after: Like in Lethal Weaponize: the payload is the personality.

lineage.reason: Quotes the Dirty Harry line 'Go ahead, make my day'.
lineage.before: Go ahead, make my day. Repeatedly.
lineage.after: Trigger's on redline. Robots can file complaints later.

lineage.reason: Paraphrases the Terminator 2 catchphrase 'Hasta la vista, baby'.
lineage.before: Hasta la vista, empty magazine.
lineage.after: Like in Speedbump: reload first, panic never.

lineage.reason: Paraphrases the Dirty Harry line 'Do you feel lucky, punk?'.
lineage.before: Feeling lucky, punk? Because I do.
lineage.after: Every shot finds the soft spot. Call it talent.

lineage.reason: 'That's gonna leave a mark' is a well-known catchphrase, and 'buddy' is generic rather than Rook.
lineage.before: That one is gonna leave a mark, buddy.
lineage.after: Found the weak spot. Scrap goes airborne, cut goes up.

lineage.reason: Paraphrases the Terminator catchphrase 'I'll be back'.
lineage.before: I'll be back. Eventually. Sturdier, too.
lineage.after: Extra hull patch. Still in one piece, mostly.

lineage.reason: Paraphrases the Predator line 'Get to the choppa'.
lineage.before: Get to the choppa, but I'm already there.
lineage.after: Like in Running Late Man: arrive first, complain after.

lineage.reason: Label is cocky but the text is a sarcastic complaint asking for help, a label/text mismatch; change the text to keep the cocky label.
lineage.before: Ow. Hull's cracked. Send patches, plural.
lineage.after: Hull's cracked. Still prettier than their robots.

lineage.reason: "Hacking time" echoes the well-known "It's ___ time" catchphrase pattern (Hammer time, It's morphin' time, "it's hacking time" meme); change the text.
lineage.before: Hacking time. Nobody touch my console.
lineage.after: Console's live. Their firewall is already nervous.

lineage.reason: "Magnets, baby" paraphrases the well-known "Yeah, bitch! Magnets!" catchphrase.
lineage.before: Loot comes to me. Magnets, baby.
lineage.after: Scrap rolls to my boots now. Magnetic personality.
